en: Therīgāthā 6.3, Khemā Therīgāthā, from the Chakkanipāta (The Chapter of Six) I am not afraid of death; I have no fear of Yama. I do not grieve for what has passed away; I do not long for what is yet to come. I dwell with a mind well-released; I am free from all attachments. I have attained peace; I am cooled and extinguished. I have seen the world as it truly is, with its arising and its passing away. Having understood this, I am now liberated; there is no further becoming for me. I have reached the end of birth; the holy life has been lived. What was to be done has been done; there is no more of this state of being. I am a woman who has crossed over the flood; I have reached the further shore. I am a woman who has attained Nibbāna; I am cooled and at peace. I am a woman who has cut the fetters; I am free from all bonds. I am a woman who has severed the stream; I am released from all attachments. I am a woman who has destroyed the taints; I am free from all defilements. I am a woman who has attained the goal; I have reached the ultimate security. I am a woman who has realized the Dhamma; I have seen the Truth. I am a woman who has transcended all suffering; I am liberated from all bonds. I am a woman who has attained the noble state; I am one who has reached the goal. “You are young and beautiful,
and I too am young and a youth;
[let us enjoy ourselves] with the fivefold musical ensemble.”
“Come, Khema, let us take our pleasure.
[He replied: “With this putrid body, diseased and fragile;”
I am repelled and ashamed;
craving for sensual pleasures has been uprooted.
Sensual pleasures are like spears and spikes.
This is the hammering down of the aggregates:
that which you call "delight in sensual pleasures" is now for me "displeasure."
Delight is destroyed everywhere,
and the mass of darkness is shattered;
know this, O Evil One!
"You are slain, O Antaka!
Paying homage to the constellations,
they tended the fire in the forest."
Not knowing things as they truly are,
fools imagined purity;
yet I, honoring it, [did not].
The perfectly enlightened one, the supreme among men;
we are liberated from all sufferings,
fulfilling the Teacher’s instruction.”
… The Elder Nun Khemā …
